author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader can narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both the directory page and the machine-readable veterinarian list accept an optional specialty named in the address and show only veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive. The narrowed page stays paged and navigable. No page control is added.
acceptance_criteria: Given /vets.html?specialty=<name>, when the page is opened, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed, and pagination applies to the filtered list.
Given /vets?specialty=<name>, when the JSON list is requested, then it carries only veterinarians holding that specialty.
Given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either surface is requested, then it matches.
Given only the beginning of a specialty's name (a prefix), when either surface is requested, then no veterinarian matches.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested, then the normal page or JSON document is returned with an empty vet list and HTTP 200.
Given a filtered directory spanning several pages, when the reader follows a pagination link, then the link carries the specialty parameter and the next page stays filtered.
Given an empty or whitespace-only specialty value, when either surface is requested, then it behaves as if the parameter were absent.
Given no specialty parameter, when either surface is requested, then it behaves as today (REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-004).
Edge case 2: a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed when any one of them matches.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface (owner deferred a visible control to a follow-up request).
Narrowing by more than one specialty at once, or by any attribute other than specialty (recorded as open questions).
A promise about a non-blank specialty padded with surrounding spaces (open question; no acceptance criterion).
notes: Narrowest readings taken per the intake's instruction; open questions recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions. REQ-VET-004 (fresh ID) reinstates the /vets JSON list as a supported surface per the owner's decision; its existing behavior is covered by the current showResourcesVetList test, so it needs no separate slice. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and is not reused. The REQ-VET-001 known-defect edge case about the unconsumed JSON route is removed, superseded by REQ-VET-004. For system-design-expert: docs/system-design.md line 12 says there is no JSON API for the primary workflows, and the Vets wrapper row carries no REQ; both may need updating for REQ-VET-004. docs/adr/README.md index needs a row for the new non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-10-25-non-goal-narrow-veterinarian-search.md (outside this agent's write scope).

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Fits the vet feature package unchanged (system-design.md § Package Structure, § Contracts): VetController binds, VetRepository queries, no service layer (feature-package ADR). Adjustments: (1) VetRepository gains specialty-narrowed derived queries, one paged for /vets.html and one unpaged for /vets, matching Specialty name whole and case-insensitively (IgnoreCase in the derived query, portable across H2/MySQL/PostgreSQL), Distinct so a vet appears once; these carry no @Cacheable (new ADR 2026-10-25-specialty-narrowing-as-uncached-query). Unnarrowed findAll methods stay as they are, cached. (2) VetController binds an optional specialty on both routes; a null, empty, or whitespace-only value is normalized to absent at binding, which architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog Web controller row classes as binding, not a business rule. The controller then delegates to the narrowed or whole read; no matching logic in the controller. (3) vetList.html page links carry specialty as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter (@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}); the absent case must not change today's links' behavior. REQ-VET-004 is docs-only here: the JSON route is now a supported surface (Overview, Vets/VetController rows, Known Defects row removed). Resolution basis: grep and file reads of VetController, VetRepository, Vet, vetList.html, ownersList.html, CacheConfiguration and the three schema.sql files (IDE oracle not connected).
integration_points: Binding, GET /vets.html: request-scoped scalars only, @RequestParam int page (existing) plus @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. No persisted type is bound.
Binding, GET /vets: @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty, request-scoped scalar. No persisted type is bound; response stays the Vets wrapper.

Double, repository boundary (ClinicServiceTests): real implementation, the existing @DataJpaTest over the embedded H2 seed data (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). Matching, case, prefix, empty-result, and multi-specialty cases are proven here against real queries.

Double, framework transport (VetControllerTests): MockMvc, the sanctioned web harness. The existing @MockitoBean VetRepository stub is tolerated legacy; a new stub for the narrowed methods is the framework-stub exception, with reason: VetRepository is a Spring Data interface with no hand-written implementation in the suite and the controller test is a @WebMvcTest slice. Controller tests assert delegation, normalization of blank to absent, model attributes, and link rendering; they do not re-prove matching.
Cache: CacheConfiguration's single vets cache is unchanged; narrowed reads bypass it.

patterns.description: paged derived query taking a criterion plus Pageable (findByLastNameStartingWith)
strip-and-default normalization of a search parameter at binding
existing findPaginated/addPaginationModel helpers to extend with the specialty; model should expose the normalized specialty for the template links

risks.risk: Veterinarian directory path scales with vet count; system-design.md § Scale and Load row 'Veterinarian directory, whole and narrowed by specialty' (unrecorded, treated as bounded).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: database-side derived query, paged at the existing page size on the HTML route, unpaged on JSON.

risks.risk: Caching narrowed reads would key the unbounded vets cache on caller-supplied text (system-design.md § Scale and Load Limits; ADR 2026-10-25-specialty-narrowing-as-uncached-query).
risks.mitigation: No @Cacheable on the narrowed repository methods; do not route them through the vets cache.

risks.risk: Template expression injection or broken links if the specialty is spliced into an href with __${...}__ preprocessing or string concatenation (system-design.md § Threat Model, template expression injection row; security-principles.md cross-site scripting row).
risks.mitigation: Emit specialty only as a link-expression parameter, which URL-encodes it; keep the page-number links' existing preprocessing free of request text. th:text keeps default escaping.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching diverging by vendor, as owner search does on PostgreSQL (system-design.md § Known Defects first row).
risks.mitigation: Case folding inside the derived query (IgnoreCase), not reliance on column collation.

risks.risk: Specialty names are not unique in any schema, so a vet joined through two specialties differing only by case could appear twice and skew page counts (system-design.md VetRepository Contracts row).
risks.mitigation: Distinct in the derived query; the count query follows it.

risks.risk: A fetch join in a hand-written query would truncate the vet's specialties to the matching one, breaking REQ-VET-001's full list and edge case 2.
risks.mitigation: Use a derived query (plain join for the predicate); Vet's eager specialties load the full set. Assert a multi-specialty vet still shows all its specialties.

risks.risk: Out-of-range page on a narrowed result (fewer pages than requested).
risks.mitigation: Behaves as the whole directory does today; no new clamp in this slice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-derived specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived queries `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` and `(String, Pageable)` in VetRepository.java, which bind it as a parameter; no query text is built from it (grep -F '@Query' / 'createQuery' / 'nativeQuery' over src/main/java finds only PetTypeRepository.java:36 `@Query("SELECT ptype FROM PetType ptype ORDER BY ptype.name")`, a constant).

Cross-site scripting / URL injection: vetList.html builds the specialty-bearing page links with Thymeleaf link-expression parameters (vetList.html:30 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`), so the value is URL-encoded and then attribute-escaped; grep -F 'utext' on vetList.html finds nothing, and VetControllerTests covers the `x-ray & imaging` -> `x-ray%20%26%20imaging` encoding.

Template preprocessing: the diff removes the `__${...}__` preprocessing from vetList.html's page links (grep -F '__${' on vetList.html now finds nothing), and the specialty never enters a preprocessing expression. The remaining preprocessing in ownersList.html:44 and the fragments is pre-existing and not on the slice's routes.

Resource exhaustion: the new specialty queries are deliberately not `@Cacheable`, so caller-supplied text cannot grow the unbounded `vets` cache (CacheConfiguration.java:37 `cm.createCache("vets", cacheConfiguration())`); the cached `findAll` paths still carry no request-derived key.

Exposed surface: no new endpoint is added. Both existing GET routes gain one optional read-only parameter that can only narrow the vet data already returned; nothing mutates state, and no request-bound object or `@ModelAttribute` target is introduced, so mass assignment does not apply.

Error handling and validation: a blank specialty normalizes to absent at binding (VetController `named` via `StringUtils::hasText`), and an unmatched specialty returns an empty list, not an error, so no exception message reaches the error page. No checks were removed or weakened.
Secrets and logging: the diff adds no credential, token, or log statement (read the full src/main diff).

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set, so no dependency changed. OWASP Dependency-Check is not configured (grep -F 'dependencyCheck' build.gradle finds nothing), so no NVD match ran. The resolved runtime classpath shows spring-boot-starter-webmvc 4.1.1, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, and hibernate-core 7.4.5.Final.

findings.description: The fix for the repeated-conditional finding regressed pagination. Each call site puts th:if and th:replace on the same , e.g. ``. Thymeleaf runs th:replace (fragment inclusion) before th:if (conditional), so the th:if is dropped and every link renders unconditionally. Observed by running `./gradlew bootRun` and fetching GET /vets.html (6 seed vets, page 1 of 2): the current page 1 renders as a link `1` beside its plain span; First and Previous render as links on page 1, Previous pointing at `/vets.html?page=0`, each beside the disabled span still shown by th:unless. Before this delta the th:if gated these links. No test pins it: VetControllerTests only asserts a page-2 href is present or absent of specialty, and never that the current page or the First/Previous link is not a link. Same defect at all five sites (page numbers, first, previous, next, last).
findings.fix: Keep the fragment, but gate it with the condition on a host that is not the th:replace element, e.g. wrap each call in ``, or move the condition into the fragment parameters. Re-render the page and confirm page 1 shows no self, First, or Previous link, and add a test asserting that.

recommendations: VetController.findPaginated takes an Optional<String> parameter; a nullable String would read more plainly. Carried from round 1, not a defect.
